questions: Should the random walk start at 0 (cumulative sum of steps) or at the first step value (i.e., the first element of steps)?

Is the seed parameter intended to seed the global random state (np.random.seed) only for the random number generation inside the function, or should it also affect any external random state after the function returns?
Should the descriptive statistics be computed on the cumulative walk values or on the individual step values (-1 or 1)?
What should be the figure size for the plot? Is a specific size required or can it be default?
Should the plot include any labels for the x-axis and y-axis, or only the title 'Random Walk'?
Are the percentiles to be computed exactly as specified (5th, 25th, 50th, 75th, 95th) using linear interpolation or another method (e.g., nearest)?
Should the function reset the matplotlib figure state (e.g., plt.close) after plotting to avoid interfering with subsequent plots?
Is the 'count' statistic in the returned dictionary supposed to be the number of steps (elements) or the number of walk values (also elements)?
